rows.title: Amazon put workers at risk at Aurora warehouse, five others nationwide, OSHA investigation finds
rows.standfirst: OSHA cited the warehouse after finding that the company put its workers at risk of musculoskeletal disorders. Amazon said an improved safety protocol has reduced injuries.

rows.title: Coloradans can defer payment on a big chunk of their rising property tax bill. Here’s how to do it.
rows.standfirst: The legislature passed a bill in 2021 allowing Coloradans to defer payment on any increase in their property tax bill over 4% by making it a lien against their home

rows.title: 780 affordable units or 3 houses? Telluride is latest Colorado town where housing, conservation clash
rows.standfirst: Push for rural affordable housing runs into battle to preserve wildlife, open space and agriculture

rows.title: Troubled oil and gas company K.P. Kauffman threatened with loss of right to do business in Colorado
rows.standfirst: State’s regulators reinstated a large fine set aside when KPK promised to clean up leaks and spills because just a tiny fraction of the work is done

rows.title: “We know”: Postal Service acknowledges growing mail problems in Colorado mountain towns
rows.standfirst: Some Colorado towns are preparing to sue to make the post office prioritize mail over last-mile deliveries for Amazon.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado business bankruptcies decline; startups on the rise
rows.standfirst: A record number of companies filed to start a business last year, but what does that mean? Plus: More money for rural startups, unemployment issues and the latest labor law poll tally

rows.title: Colorado considers using public land for affordable workforce housing
rows.standfirst: The legislature is considering a new proposal to free up vacant parcels of state-owned land that could be leased or sold at a discount for affordable housing projects

rows.title: The annual Warren Miller ski movie isn’t going anywhere, despite reports to the contrary
rows.standfirst: In 2020, Outside acquired Warren Miller Entertainment alongside SKI, Climbing, Backpacker and 12 other magazines, events and brands

rows.title: Colorado’s governor wants to reduce your utility bill. Don’t expect a big decrease anytime soon.
rows.standfirst: The requests Gov. Jared Polis made Monday will take a year or more to take effect. They are intended to help Coloradans next winter.

rows.title: A private equity firm closed one of Colorado’s few birth centers. The community brought it back.
rows.standfirst: A private equity firm bought Seasons Midwifery and Birth Center in Thornton and then shut it down. It’s now been resurrected as a nonprofit.

rows.title: PUC responds to Polis’ call for utility relief: “We certainly don’t have all the answers now”
rows.standfirst: The regulatory body, which reports to the governor, said that it’ll try to move forward on fixing a system that’s put many Coloradans in financial distress with sky-high utility bills this winter

rows.title: What’s Working: When Colorado’s tight labor market met the state’s housing affordability issue
rows.standfirst: So many job openings, so few “affordable” houses for sale. Colorado Realtors met to discuss. Plus: Workers aren’t “on the couch,” labor demographics are changing, more!

rows.title: Colorado Democrats are turning 2023 into the year of housing. But should the state wade into local land decisions?
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers may limit local land-use directives to promote housing density. Also on the docket: rent control, eviction limitations and transit-oriented development.

rows.title: Colorado, 10 other states consider “right to repair” for farming equipment
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers introduced bills that would force manufacturers to provide the tools, software, parts and manuals needed for farmers to do their own repair

rows.title: Centura Health, one of Colorado’s largest hospital systems, announces its breakup
rows.standfirst: CommonSpirit Health and AdventHealth say they will manage their hospitals separately

rows.title: Metro Denver median home prices finally dropped after two years of unprecedented growth
rows.standfirst: After a hectic two years of unprecedented home price increases, the median sales price stayed the same in Colorado, dropped in metro Denver, and rose in other parts of the state in January

rows.title: Xcel may have to refund connection fees for Colorado homeowners whose solar projects were delayed
rows.standfirst: Backlog of getting home systems linked to the grid reached a peak in January. Xcel says it’s catching up but also blames developers.

rows.title: Loveland Ski Area patrollers, paramedics seek to unionize in push for better wages
rows.standfirst: If successful, Loveland would join a growing list of ski areas with unionized patrollers in Colorado’s consolidating resort industry

rows.title: Meat plant cleaning service fined $1.5M for hiring minors, including at JBS in Greeley
rows.standfirst: Labor Department says one of the country’s largest cleaning services for food processing companies employed more than 100 children in dangerous jobs

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver inflation falls to 6.4%, which means we still have high inflation
rows.standfirst: Gas prices are back over $4 a gallon but a bigger inflation culprit is housing prices. Plus: Fair Workweek bill on pause, more chips for Colorado Springs.

rows.title: Colorado considers trapping greenhouse gases in abandoned oil and gas wells with biochar
rows.standfirst: Colorado lawmakers gave initial approval Thursday for a study to assess whether biochar would work to plug defunct wells

rows.title: Criminal charges against preschool teachers, closure of child care center tore a Colorado town apart
rows.standfirst: Parents, now scrambling to find alternative care after the abrupt closure of The Schoolhouse in Poncha Springs, are accusing authorities of overreacting to reports of a 5-year-old touching younger classmates

rows.title: Ramen, sesame balls and croffles: Denver’s new (but not first) Asian Food Week just began
rows.standfirst: How the event came to be, past attempts and some tips on the best way to tackle the five-day affair celebrating the Asian-food community.

rows.title: Cotter Mill cleanup company says it is insolvent, will stop work on Cañon City Superfund site
rows.standfirst: Colorado Legacy Land was paid in 2018 to take over remediation of one of the slowest Superfund cleanups in the U.S. and a uranium mine leaking into Ralston Creek west of Denver

rows.title: Colorado goes analog to boost affordable internet program after just 23% of eligible households join
rows.standfirst: The federal Affordable Connectivity Program provides up to $30 a month to pay for internet service. State participation rate is lower than the national rate.

rows.title: Court of Appeals rules in favor of Garfield County, upholding notice of violation against quarry
rows.standfirst: The decision affirmed the county’s right to regulate the mining company and represents a win for community activists opposed to the expansion of its Glenwood Springs quarry.

rows.title: Railroad’s plan to haul waxy crude through Colorado’s mountains needs $2 billion in government-approved bonds
rows.standfirst: Opposition to taxpayers helping foot the bill for Uinta Basin Railway’s “massive carbon bomb” is lining up

rows.title: Colorado grocery, convenience stores uncork wine sales starting March 1
rows.standfirst: Trader Joe’s, Safeway and King Soopers all plan to immediately sell wine in their stores.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado is more transparent about wages than any other state
rows.standfirst: Updates to the Equal Pay for Equal Work law have begun. Plus: Homeownership, 487 people waiting 10+ weeks for unemployment benefits, labor department jobs and more!

rows.title: How Denver-area governments are spending the $41 million they received from the Broncos sale
rows.standfirst: The seven counties and 40 municipalities in the Metro Stadium District, which helped fund Broncos stadium, are starting to distribute refunds from last year’s $4.65 billion sale to the Walton-Penner Group

rows.title: Colorado is so short on workers for people with disabilities that it’s starting a marketing campaign to find more
rows.standfirst: Aging parents who care for adult children with intellectual and developmental disabilities are struggling to find room in day programs as a staffing crisis results in cut hours, long waitlists

rows.title: After capping insulin copays, Colorado sets its sights on EpiPens
rows.standfirst: A proposed state law would cap out-of-pocket copays at $60 for a two-pack of epinephrine autoinjectors, which retail for $636 in Denver.

rows.title: Troubled K.P. Kauffman violated state order to stop selling its oil and gas
rows.standfirst: KPK says it must sell oil and gas or its 1,200 wells may end up orphaned. Regulators say they don’t appreciate the threats.

rows.title: At the University of Colorado, a sports betting company is aiming its pitch at students
rows.standfirst: Until January, the university received a $30 fee when anyone, including a student, signed up at the PointsBet site using a CU promotional code

frame: Fixed public category union, followed by frozen economic-title inclusion screen
